findings.description: The "House rules worth knowing before you write code" section restates AGENTS.md's rules (Node-free output, near-zero deps, naming taxonomy, comments, git workflow) near-verbatim in a second file — exactly the multi-file drift risk this project's own README calls out as the problem agent-init solves. A one-line pointer to AGENTS.md would avoid having two places to keep in sync.

Two of the four new lede bullets ("Node-free output", "No pretending") restate the "Design in one table" rows below almost word-for-word within the same document (compare lines ~59 and ~64), so a reader hits the same fact twice within 40 lines.

SECURITY.md's "I will confirm receipt, and credit you in the advisory" is the only first-person voice among the new docs in this PR; CONTRIBUTING.md instead uses the collective "us" ("any breakage lands on us first"). The two new files disagree on solo-maintainer vs. team framing, which reads as unintentional.

The closing "Reporting a bug" section restates in prose exactly what bug_report.yml already encodes as structured fields, and the same "paste doctor --json" instruction is repeated a third time in README.md's new "Contributing" section — three sites with no cross-reference to keep in sync if the bug-report format changes.

The intro "agent-init doctor --json answers most of this. Paste it below and skip the fields it covers" overpromises: doctor's JSON output (jq presence, hooks scaffolding, per-tool wiring/blocking) doesn't actually cover any of the form's required fields (what-happened, area, env) or even fully cover the optional tools field (no version info), so a contributor taking "skip the fields it covers" literally has nothing they can actually skip.

The "Security vulnerability" contact link points at /security/advisories/new, which only resolves to a usable private report form if "Private vulnerability reporting" is enabled in the repo's Security settings — a setting this diff can't confirm and is worth the maintainer checking out-of-band.

refuted_findings.description: SECURITY.md states the CI review model's job holds read-only permissions and a separate job posts, which the conventions reviewer read as contradicting docs/design/0001-architecture.md decision 21's "worth doing, not done here" sentence about splitting the poster into its own job.
refuted_findings.refutation: Validated directly against .github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml (confirmed unmodified by this PR). The claude-review job's permissions block (lines 75-78) grants only contents:read, pull-requests:read, issues:read; a separate post-review job (lines 272-281) holds pull-requests:write. The workflow's own inline comments (lines 72-74, 232-234) state this split as current design fact: "the poster job writes them... this job's token... cannot write to the PR at all." SECURITY.md's claim matches the actually-shipped pipeline exactly. The ADR's "not done here" sentence is stale prose left over from the same squash-merge commit (bcd7d72, PR #17) that actually shipped the split — a pre-existing documentation inconsistency between the ADR and the workflow, not something this PR introduces or misdescribes.
